what_its_for: Efinaconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the toenails (also called onychomycosis). It works by killing the fungus that causes the infection, helping your nails grow back healthy and clear.
how_to_take: Efinaconazole comes as a 10% solution that you apply directly to your affected toenails. Use the small brush that comes with the bottle to apply a thin, even coat over the entire toenail surface, including under the tip of the nail and on the skin right around it. Let it dry completely before putting on socks or shoes. Do not wash the treated area for at least 10 minutes after applying. Apply it once every day, preferably at the same time each day.
dosing: Apply the solution to all affected toenails once daily for 48 weeks (about 11 months). Use only the amount needed to cover each nail — do not apply extra thinking it will work faster. This medicine is for external (outside) use only. Never swallow it.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply your dose, apply it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your normal schedule. Never apply two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and open flames — this medicine is flammable. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Do not get this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or vagina. Avoid applying nail polish, gel nails, or other nail cosmetics to the treated nails during treatment, as these can block the medicine from working. Avoid exposing the treated area to open fire or flames right after application since the medicine is flammable. Do not let other people use your bottle.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice severe redness, swelling, blistering, burning, or skin peeling around your nail that seems worse than usual. Also call your doctor if you accidentally get the medicine in your eyes or mouth, if your symptoms do not improve after several months of use, or if you develop any new or unusual symptoms. Seek emergency help if you accidentally swallow any of this medicine.
when_it_works: Toenail fungal infections take a long time to treat because nails grow slowly. You may not see noticeable improvement for several months. It can take up to 48 weeks (about 11 months) of daily use to see the full benefit. Do not stop using the medicine early even if it seems like nothing is happening — stopping too soon can allow the fungus to come back. Talk to your doctor if you have questions about your progress.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. The safety of efinaconazole during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. This medicine is not approved for use in children under 6 years of age. Elderly patients can generally use this medicine safely, but should tell their doctor about all other medicines they are taking.
